Tomato Friselle

Puglian friselle lightly moistened and topped with tomatoes, black olives, basil, oregano, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 friselle
1 1/3 cups chopped ripe tomatoes
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
about 1/2 cup pitted black olives
8 basil leaves
1 tsp dried oregano
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 cup cold water for moistening

Preparation

1. Pour the water into a shallow dish.

2. Dip each frisella quickly for 5–10 seconds.

3. Drain and arrange on a serving platter.

4. Cut the tomatoes into small pieces.

5. Put them in a bowl.

6. Add the olive oil, salt, pepper, and oregano.

7. Add the olives.

8. Tear the basil by hand.

9. Add it to the tomatoes.

10. Toss gently.

11. Spoon the topping over the friselle.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Moisten the friselle only briefly so the surface softens while the interior retains some crunch.

Bari Sgagliozze

Fried polenta triangles that are crisp outside and soft inside.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups water
1 1/2 cups instant polenta
1 1/3 tsp fine salt, divided
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Bring the water to a boil.

2. Add about 3/4 teaspoon salt.

3. Slowly stream in the polenta while stirring continuously.

4. Cook for 3–4 minutes or according to the package directions.

5. Pour the polenta into a rectangular pan.

6. Smooth to about 3/8 inch thick.

7. Cool for 4–5 hours.

8. Unmold the polenta.

9. Cut first into squares and then into triangles.

10. Heat the oil to 355°F.

11. Fry 3–4 triangles at a time.

12. Turn after several minutes.

13. Continue until deeply golden and crisp.

14. Drain on paper towels.

15. Sprinkle with the remaining salt.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

The polenta must be completely cold and firm before cutting or the triangles can break apart in the oil.

Bari Popizze

Very soft Bari-style yeasted dough fritters fried by the spoonful.

Yield: about 30 pieces

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water, room temperature
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 level tsp sugar
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a large bowl.

2. Dissolve the yeast in about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon water.

3. Add it to the flour.

4. Gradually add the remaining water.

5. Add the sugar.

6. Add the salt.

7. Beat the dough vigorously by hand or with a sturdy whisk for about 10 minutes.

8. Continue until fluid, elastic, and uniform.

9. Cover.

10. Let rise for 2 hours.

11. Heat the oil to 350–355°F.

12. Wet two spoons.

13. Scoop small portions of dough.

14. Slide them into the oil.

15. Fry only a few at a time for about 3 minutes, turning until golden.

16. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Vigorous mixing incorporates air into the dough and contributes to the light interior of the popizze.

Salento Pittule

Soft Salento-style yeasted dough fritters fried until puffed and golden.

Yield: about 50 pieces

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water, room temperature
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
4 1/4 cups peanut or high-oleic sunflower oil for frying

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a large bowl.

2. Crumble the yeast into the flour.

3. Add the water gradually.

4. Mix with a sturdy spatula or your hands.

5. Add the salt halfway through mixing.

6. Continue adding the water.

7. Work vigorously for several minutes until the batter is elastic, uniform, soft, and sticky.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for about 2 hours, until clearly increased in volume.

10. Heat the oil to 340–355°F.

11. Wet or oil two spoons.

12. Scoop small portions of dough.

13. Slide them into the oil.

14. Fry only a few at a time for about 2–3 minutes.

15. Turn during frying.

16. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Do not add flour after rising. The dough should remain very soft to produce light, airy pittule.

Gratinated Mussels

Puglian mussels gratinated with breadcrumbs, Pecorino, garlic, parsley, and oregano.

Yield: 4 servings

2 1/4 lb mussels
about 3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp breadcrumbs
1 cup finely grated Pecorino
2 garlic cloves
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 tsp dried oregano
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 cup strained mussel liquid
1/3 tsp fine salt, only if needed

Preparation

1. Clean the mussels thoroughly.

2. Put them in a saucepan with 1 garlic clove.

3. Cover and cook until they open.

4. Discard any that remain closed.

5. Remove the empty half of each shell.

6. Strain the mussel liquid carefully.

7. Mix the breadcrumbs, Pecorino, remaining minced garlic, parsley, and oregano.

8. Taste the mixture before adding any salt.

9. Arrange the mussels on a baking sheet.

10. Spoon the filling over each mussel.

11. Drizzle with the olive oil.

12. Spoon the strained mussel liquid over the tops.

13. Preheat the broiler to 400°F.

14. Broil for 4–5 minutes, until golden.

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

The mussel liquid and Pecorino are both salty, so additional salt may not be necessary.

Polpo alla Pignata

Salento octopus slowly cooked in earthenware with tomatoes, potatoes, onion, garlic, white wine, parsley, and chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 cleaned octopus, about 2 1/4 lb
3 1/3 cups cherry tomatoes
about 3 1/3 cups potato chunks
1 red onion, sliced
1 garlic clove, minced
1 small chile
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Rinse and dry the octopus.

2. Cut the head and tentacles into large pieces.

3. Peel the potatoes.

4. Cut them into even chunks.

5. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

6. Heat the olive oil in an earthenware pot or heavy saucepan.

7. Add the onion, garlic, and chile.

8. Cook for 4–5 minutes.

9. Add the octopus.

10. Sauté for 3–4 minutes.

11. Pour in the wine.

12. Let the alcohol evaporate for 2 minutes.

13. Add the tomatoes and potatoes.

14. Cover.

15. Bring to a gentle boil without adding water.

16. Reduce the heat.

17. Cook for about 1 hour, stirring gently every 15 minutes.

18. Add the salt only near the end.

19. Turn off the heat.

20. Add the parsley.

21. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Service

Serve very hot with toasted bread.

Chef's note

The octopus should cook in its own released liquid. Added water dilutes the sauce and is unnecessary if the pot remains covered.

Puglian baked anchovies with stale bread, garlic, parsley, capers, oregano, vinegar, and olive oil.

1 tsp dried oregano, optional

1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil

1. Clean the anchovies, removing the heads and innards.

2. Butterfly them and remove the central bones.

3. Rinse briefly.

4. Dry very thoroughly.

5. Lightly grease an earthenware or baking dish with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

6. Arrange the fillets in a radial pattern.

7. Crumble the bread coarsely.

8. Mix it with the garlic, parsley, capers, oregano, and pepper.

10. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

11. Sprinkle with the vinegar.

Chef's note

Taste before adding salt; the capers and anchovies can provide enough salinity on their own.

Onion Calzone

Bari-style calzone filled with sponsali onions, olives, raisins, anchovies, and cheese.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
3 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp warm water
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
about 2 1/2 tsp fresh yeast
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 6 cups sliced sponsali or mild spring onions
1/3 cup raisins
about 1/3 cup rinsed salt-packed anchovies
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano or Pecorino
30 pitted black olives
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 cup water
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Add the yeast water, wine, and olive oil.

4. Knead for about 15 minutes.

5. Add the salt during the final minutes.

6. Form a ball.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise for about 2 hours.

9. Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes.

10. Drain and dry.

11. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet.

12. Add the sponsali.

13. Add the water.

14. Cook over medium-low heat for about 30 minutes.

15. Add the salt and pepper.

16. Add the cheese, olives, raisins, and anchovies.

17. Continue cooking until the pan is completely dry.

18. Cool completely.

19. Divide the dough into two pieces.

20. Roll into two thin 11-inch disks.

21. Line a pan with the first disk.

22. Add the cooled filling.

23. Cover with the second disk.

24. Seal and fold the edges.

25. Bake in a preheated 445°F oven for at least 30 minutes, until golden.

26. Broil for 1–2 minutes if needed.

Service

Rest for 15 minutes and serve warm.

Chef's note

The filling must be completely dry and cool before it goes into the dough or the bottom crust will stay damp.

Scapece Gallipolina

Gallipoli fried small fish layered with stale bread soaked in saffron vinegar.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 3/4 lb small frying fish
about 20 cups coarse stale bread crumb
4 1/4 cups white-wine vinegar
3 packets saffron, about 1/2 tsp threads or powder
1 cup durum or all-purpose flour
4 1/4 cups extra-virgin olive oil for frying
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Dry the small fish thoroughly.

2. Coat lightly in flour.

3. Shake off the excess.

4. Heat the oil to 350°F.

5. Fry the fish in batches until golden.

6. Drain on paper towels.

7. Season with salt.

8. Cool completely.

9. Pour the vinegar into a large bowl.

10. Dissolve the saffron in it.

11. Crumble the stale bread.

12. Moisten it thoroughly with the saffron vinegar until fully saturated.

13. Make one layer of soaked bread in a tall container.

14. Cover with a thin layer of fried fish.

15. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used.

16. Finish with a bread layer.

17. Cover.

18. Refrigerate for at least 24 hours.

Service

Serve cold or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The 24-hour rest is essential because it allows the saffron vinegar to penetrate both the bread and fish and develop the traditional flavor.

Palermo Arancine

Round Palermo rice balls with saffron rice, meat-and-pea ragù, batter, and breadcrumbs.

Yield: about 20 arancine

Ingredients

For the rice
5 cups Originario or short-grain rice
8 1/2 cups water
about 1 1/2 tbsp vegetable bouillon concentrate
2 saffron packets, about 1/8 tsp
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For the ragù
1 1/8 lb ground beef

1 1/3 cups peas

1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1 bay leaf
3/4 tsp fine salt

about 1 1/4 cups diced well-drained primosale or mozzarella

1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups cold water
1 large egg
1/2 tsp fine salt
2 1/2 cups breadcrumbs

For frying
4 1/4 cups peanut oil

Preparation

1. Put the rice, water, vegetable bouillon, and saffron in a large saucepan.

2. Add the salt and pepper.

3. Bring to a boil.

4. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until the rice absorbs all of the water.

5. Spread the rice in a thin layer on a baking sheet.

6. Cool completely.

7. For the ragù, heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

8. Add the onion.

9. Cook for 5 minutes.

10. Add the ground beef.

11. Brown for 7–8 minutes.

12. Pour in the wine.

13. Let the alcohol evaporate.

14. Add the tomato sauce, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.

15. Cook over low heat for 30 minutes.

16. Add the peas.

17. Continue for another 15 minutes, until the ragù is very thick.

18. Remove the bay leaf.

19. Cool completely.

20. Make the batter by whisking the flour, water, egg, and salt until smooth and fluid.

21. Lightly wet your hands.

22. Take one portion of rice and make a hollow in your palm.

23. Put about 1 heaping tablespoon ragù in the center and, if using, one cube of primosale or mozzarella.

24. Cover with more rice.

25. Compact into a ball.

26. Dip each arancina in the batter.

27. Let excess batter drip away.

28. Coat in breadcrumbs.

29. Heat the oil to 350°F.

30. Fry only a few at a time for 5–7 minutes, turning until evenly golden.

31. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Rest for 3–5 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

The rice and ragù must be completely cold before shaping; warm components make the arancine difficult to compact.

Yield: about 10 panelle

Ingredients

1 cup chickpea flour
1 cup water
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying
1 lemon, optional for serving
1/3 tsp fine salt for finishing

Preparation

1. Put the chickpea flour, water, salt, pepper, and parsley in a saucepan.

2. Whisk thoroughly while still cold.

3. Set the pan over low heat.

4. Cook, stirring continuously, for 15–20 minutes.

5. Continue until the mixture is very thick, smooth, and pulls away from the sides.

6. Immediately spread the hot mixture over flat plates or a smooth surface in a thin layer.

7. Cool for about 15 minutes.

8. Carefully lift off the panelle.

9. Cut into the desired shape.

10. Heat the oil to 340–350°F.

11. Fry only a few panelle at a time until puffed and golden.

12. Drain on paper towels.

13. Sprinkle with the finishing salt.

Service

Serve immediately, with lemon wedges if desired.

Chef's note

Spread the mixture while still piping hot. It firms quickly as it cools and becomes difficult to spread thinly.

Palermo Potato Croquettes

Palermo potato croquettes made only with potatoes, parsley, and mint, fried without breading.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 1 lb floury mature potatoes
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Wash the potatoes.

2. Put them whole and unpeeled in a pot of cold salted water.

3. Bring to a boil.

4. Cook until tender.

5. Drain.

6. Cool completely in a colander, preferably overnight.

7. Peel the cold potatoes.

8. Pass them through a potato ricer.

9. Add the parsley, mint, salt, and pepper.

10. Mix quickly without overworking the potatoes.

11. Lightly oil your hands.

12. Shape into elongated croquettes.

13. Arrange on a tray lined with a clean kitchen towel.

14. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

15. Heat the oil to 375°F.

16. Fry only a few croquettes at a time for about 2 minutes, until deeply golden.

17. Drain with a slotted spoon.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Cooling the potatoes for many hours dries them and concentrates the starch, allowing the croquettes to hold together without eggs or breading.

Sicilian sardines rolled with breadcrumbs, raisins, pine nuts, anchovies, parsley, and bay leaves.

Serve hot or warm.

Do not overfill the sardines; a compact roll holds its shape better during baking.

Ingredients

1 round purple eggplant, about 1 1/2 lb

2/3 cup peeled tomatoes

1/2 cup raisins

1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

1. Cut the eggplant into even cubes.

2. Put it in a colander.

3. Sprinkle with the coarse salt.

4. Place a weight on top.

5. Let drain for about 2 hours.

6. Rinse briefly.

7. Dry very thoroughly.

8. Heat the peanut oil to 350°F.

9. Fry the eggplant in small batches until golden.

10. Drain on paper towels.

11. Soak the raisins in cold water for 10 minutes.

12. Drain.

13. Blanch the celery for 3 minutes.

14. Drain and cut into pieces.

15. Chop the tomatoes and halve the olives.

16. Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a wide skillet.

17. Add the celery.

18. Sauté for 2–3 minutes.

19. Add the capers, raisins, olives, pine nuts, tomatoes, and basil.

20. Cook for 5 minutes.

21. Add the fried eggplant.

22. Season with fine salt and pepper.

23. Cook for another 3 minutes.

24. Dissolve the sugar in the vinegar.

25. Pour it into the skillet.

26. Increase the heat slightly.

27. Cook for another 10 minutes, until the sharp vinegar aroma softens.

Service

Rest for at least 2 hours and serve at room temperature.

Caponata improves after resting because the sweet-and-sour dressing penetrates the vegetables and the flavors balance.

Stigghiola

Palermo-style lamb intestines wrapped around scallions and parsley stems and grilled over coals.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 lb very fresh lamb intestines, already purged
1 unwaxed lemon
1/2 cup fresh parsley with intact stems
4 small scallions
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Rinse the intestines under cold running water.

2. Fill a bowl with cold water.

3. Add half of the salt and the juice of half the lemon.

4. Soak the intestines for 15 minutes.

5. Rinse very thoroughly again.

6. Dry.

7. Clean the scallions and keep them whole.

8. Divide the parsley stems into four small bundles.

9. Pair one scallion with one parsley bundle.

10. Wrap one portion of intestine tightly around the aromatics from end to end.

11. Repeat to make 4 stigghiola.

12. Prepare medium-hot coals with no direct flame.

13. Put the stigghiola on the grill.

14. Cook for 15–20 minutes.

15. Turn frequently for even browning.

16. Season gradually with the remaining salt and pepper.

17. Continue until the exterior is deeply browned and crisp and no soft or wet sections remain.

Service

Serve immediately with wedges from the remaining lemon.

Chef's note

Use steady medium heat without flames. Dripping fat can cause flare-ups that burn the outside before the interior cooks completely.

Ribollita

Tuscan bean-and-vegetable soup with cannellini beans, Tuscan kale, Savoy cabbage, and stale bread.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 cups cooked cannellini beans
7 cups bean cooking liquid or water
1 small onion, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, minced
2 carrots, diced
1 celery stalk, diced
1 potato, diced
about 3 cups sliced Tuscan kale
about 4 cups sliced Savoy cabbage
1 tbsp tomato paste
about 4 cups thinly sliced stale Tuscan-style bread
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 1/4 tsp fine salt, divided
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Blend half of the beans with 1 cup of the measured cooking liquid.

2. Reserve the purée and the remaining whole beans separately.

3. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot.

4. Add the onion and garlic with about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

5. Cook over low heat for 5 minutes.

6. Add the carrots, celery, and potato.

7. Stir for 3 minutes.

8. Add the Tuscan kale and Savoy cabbage.

9. Pour in the remaining cooking liquid.

10. Add the tomato paste, remaining salt, and pepper.

11. Bring to a gentle simmer.

12. Cook for about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.

13. Add the bean purée.

14. Cook for another 20 minutes, stirring frequently.

15. Add the whole beans.

16. Cook for another 10 minutes.

17. Add the sliced bread.

18. Stir and cook for another 10 minutes.

19. Turn off the heat.

20. Rest for at least 30 minutes.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil. For traditional ribollita, cool completely, refrigerate, and reheat the next day until the soup returns to a simmer.

Chef's note

The cannellini purée thickens the soup naturally; stir frequently after adding it so the bottom does not catch.

Maremma Acquacotta

Maremma soup with onions, celery, tomatoes, poached eggs, Tuscan bread, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 medium white or yellow onions, thinly sliced
1 whole leafy celery bunch, about 4 cups sliced
4 1/4 cups peeled tomatoes
4 basil leaves
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
4 1/4 cups water
4 large eggs
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano
4 slices stale Tuscan-style bread
1 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp dried chile

Preparation

1. Put the onions and celery in a large pot.

2. Add the water, olive oil, salt, chile, and basil.

3. Bring to a gentle simmer.

4. Cook uncovered over medium-low heat until nearly all of the water has evaporated and the vegetables are very soft, about 35–45 minutes.

5. Add the peeled tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon.

6. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons hot water.

7. Cook for another 20 minutes.

8. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

9. Make four small spaces in the soup.

10. Crack one egg into each.

11. Cover.

12. Cook for 3–5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft.

13. Put one slice of stale bread in each bowl.

14. Sprinkle the bread with Parmigiano.

Service

Ladle the soup over the bread and place one poached egg in each serving.

Chef's note

The long first cooking concentrates the sweetness of the onions and celery; do not add the tomatoes until the initial water has nearly evaporated.

21. Bring the broth back to a boil.

22. Add all of the greens.

23. Cook for 5–7 minutes.

24. Add the remaining salt only if needed.

25. Return the meats to the pot.

26. Heat for 2 minutes.

Service

Serve very hot with a balanced portion of meat, greens, and broth.

Skimming fat throughout the long cooking keeps the soup rich without making it heavy.

Neapolitan Soffritto Soup

Neapolitan spicy pork-offal soup with lard, red wine, concentrated tomato, bay, rosemary, and chile.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

4 lb mixed pork offal such as lung, trachea, heart, and spleen
1 tbsp olive oil
7 tbsp lard
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry red wine
3 tbsp tomato paste concentrate
1/4 cup water for diluting the concentrate
about 3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp double-concentrated tomato paste
1 bay leaf
1 small chile
1 rosemary sprig
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
2 cups plus 2 tbsp hot water, plus another 2 cups plus 2 tbsp available if needed

Preparation

1. Cut the offal into pieces about 3/4 inch wide.

2. Soak in plenty of fresh water for 2 hours.

3. Change the water at least twice.

4. Drain.

5. Dry very thoroughly.

6. Heat the olive oil and lard in a heavy saucepan.

7. Add the offal.

8. Brown over high heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until deeply colored.

9. Pour in the red wine.

10. Let the alcohol evaporate.

11. Dilute the first tomato concentrate in the measured water.

12. Add it with the remaining concentrated tomato.

13. Add the bay leaf, chile, rosemary, and salt.

14. Cook for 5 minutes.

15. Add the hot water.

16. Bring to a gentle simmer.

17. Reduce the heat.

18. Cover partially.

19. Cook for about 2 hours.

20. Stir every 15 minutes.

21. If the sauce becomes too thick before the offal is tender, add the remaining hot water in 1/2-cup portions.

22. Remove the bay leaf and rosemary.

Service

Serve very hot with rustic bread.

Chef's note

Browning the offal thoroughly before adding tomato and water develops the deep flavor characteristic of soffritto.

Neapolitan Mussel Soup

Neapolitan Holy Thursday seafood soup with octopus, mussels, clams, shrimp, sea snails, friselle, and spicy red “’o russ” oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the soup
3 1/4 lb octopus
2 1/4 lb very fresh mussels
7/8 lb purged clams
8 whole shrimp or scampi
about 1/2 lb small sea snails
8–12 olive-oil friselle
4 garlic cloves
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil for the separate seafood cooking

For the spicy “’o russ” oil
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 dried red chiles, crumbled
2 tbsp tomato paste
1/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Prepare the spicy oil first.

2. Put the olive oil, chile, tomato paste, and salt in a heavy small saucepan.

3. Heat over the lowest setting for 15 minutes without letting the tomato paste fry.

4. Stir regularly.

5. Turn off the heat and cool.

6. Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil.

7. Dip the octopus tentacles into the boiling water three times to curl them.

8. Lower the entire octopus into the water.

9. Reduce the heat.

10. Cook for 40–45 minutes.

11. Turn off the heat.

12. Rest the octopus in its broth for 10 minutes.

13. Remove and cut into pieces.

14. Reserve the broth.

15. Clean the mussels thoroughly.

16. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil with 1 garlic clove in a skillet.

17. Add the mussels.

18. Cover and cook until they open.

19. Discard any that remain closed.

20. Strain their liquid and add it to the octopus broth.

21. Repeat with the clams using another 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 garlic clove.

22. Sauté the shrimp or scampi with 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 garlic clove for 2–3 minutes.

23. Sauté the sea snails with the final 1 tablespoon olive oil and garlic clove for 3–4 minutes.

24. Reheat the octopus broth enriched with the strained shellfish liquids.

25. Dip each frisella in the hot broth for only a few seconds.

26. Arrange 2–3 friselle in each bowl.

27. Add the octopus, mussels, clams, shrimp, and sea snails.

28. Drizzle each serving with 1–2 tablespoons spicy red oil.

Service

Serve immediately while very hot.

Chef's note

The friselle should soften only on the outside while remaining somewhat firm in the center; dip them in the broth for only a few seconds.
